newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy futures mixed amid thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy futures mixed amid thin trade.

text.p: U.S. energy futures prices were mixed on ACCESS trade Monday, with heating oil the only gainer in a market thinned by Tuesday's crude expiry and today's Martin Luther King holiday, traders said.
February NYMEX crude eased 11 cents a barrel overnight to $25.12, under pressure from profit-taking as traders liquidated their February positions and bought March, brokers said.
"It could be some length trying to get out," a trader said.
Crude activity stood around 766 lots for all months, with 348 traded in February and 386 in March.
NYMEX February heating oil rose, but traders were uncertain of fundamentals since activity was thin at 150 lots total, and 99 in the front month.
"There's not too much giving direction," a trader said, attibuted range-bound "heat" to moderating winter weather in the key Northeastern U.S. and adequate distillate inventories.
The contract rose 0.26 cents a gallon to 67.20 cents.
Gasoline futures edged down 0.03 cents a gallon to 67.20 cents with 23 lots traded in total.
